name: MALTA

flag.title: Flag of Malta
flag.note: White & red with George Cross top-left

lead: Malta is a tiny island in the Mediterranean Sea. You can drive across it in 30 minutes. It has temples older than the Pyramids. People speak a language found nowhere else.
geo: Malta lies between Sicily and North Africa. Three of its islands have people. They are made almost entirely of golden limestone. Waves have carved sea caves, sheer cliffs and fine harbours.
Malta covers just 316 km², yet nearly 575,000 people live here. It is one of the most crowded countries in the world. The sun shines over 300 days a year.
animals: Malta's national bird is the Blue Rock Thrush, a cobalt-blue songbird that nests on sea cliffs. Each autumn thousands of migrating birds cross the island.
Each autumn lampuki (mahi-mahi) swim in golden-green schools. Fishermen lure them with floating palm-leaf mats. Colourful luzzu boats bring in octopus and sea bream.
culture: Maltese culture mixes Arab, Italian and British ways. Every village throws a summer festa, a loud street party with fireworks and brass bands.
Rabbit stew is the national dish. Pastizzi, flaky ricotta pastries, are the favourite snack. Everyone speaks English, but locals slip into musical Maltese.
history: Malta's story goes back 7,000 years. Its Megalithic Temples, built around 3600 BC, are among the oldest freestanding buildings on Earth. Phoenicians, Romans, Arabs and Normans came later.
The Knights of St John arrived in 1530. After the Great Siege of 1565, they built Valletta. In World War II bombs fell on Malta for 154 days.
wows: Malta's temples date to 3600 BC, older than Stonehenge and the Egyptian Pyramids.
Valletta has only 5,000 residents, the fewest of any EU capital.
Maltese is the only Semitic language written in the Latin alphabet.
Malta has about 365 churches, nearly one for each day of the year.
King George VI gave the George Cross to the whole island in 1942.
The Ħal Saflieni Hypogeum is the world's only known prehistoric underground burial site.
In 1239 Emperor Frederick II sent 18 falconers to Malta for its falcons.

myths.fact: It is independent. It left British rule in 1964 and became a republic in 1974.

myths.myth: Maltese is a dialect of Arabic
myths.fact: Maltese is its own language. It borrowed many words from Italian and English.
